articles.title: The Amazon tax
articles.titleZh: 亚马逊税
articles.author: herbertl

zh.thesis: 亚马逊的搜索广告不是税，而是合法的偷窃，每年拿走五百多亿美元，最后买单的是消费者。
paragraphs: 亚马逊每周从搜索广告赚近十亿美元。作者说这不是税——税会带来公共福利——这是合法的偷窃，钱多到够给每个员工发 3.5 万美元奖金还有剩。
你搜空气炸锅，亚马逊原本知道哪款评价最好、退货最少。广告的唯一作用，是让你改买另一款，或者把你本来就打算买的那款再推一次。搜索因此变差了。
最好的那款也得买广告自卫。作者的出版商买下「Seth Godin The Knot」这个搜索词，每次点击付一美元，可读者本来就是要去买这本书的。
结果就是：品牌不如点击预算重要，商家宁可做廉价品也要省钱买点击；平台则有动力让自然搜索结果更差，逼你买更多广告。亚马逊曾经靠低价服务顾客，现在这套系统为谁而设，很清楚。

en.thesis: Amazon's search ads are legal theft, not a tax: they take more than $50 billion a year, and customers foot the bill.
paragraphs: Amazon takes nearly a billion dollars a week from search ads. The author calls it legal theft, not a tax — taxes buy public benefits — and it is enough to hand every employee a $35,000 cash bonus and still have change left over.

Search for an air fryer and Amazon already knows which model reviews best and gets returned least. The ads exist only to make you pick a different one, or to nudge you back to the one you had already chosen. Search is worse because of them.

Even the best model has to buy ads now, just to defend sales it was already entitled to. The author's publisher is running the search 'Seth Godin The Knot'; it costs about a dollar a click to show you an ad for a book you were already going to buy.

The side effects are perverse. If brand matters less than a click budget, producers cheapen their products to free up money for ads. And the platform has an incentive to make organic results worse, pushing you toward more ads. Amazon used to serve customers by lowering prices; it is clear who this system serves now.

articles.title: Everything You Believe About Taking a Full Course of Antibiotics and Bacterial Resistance Is Wrong
articles.titleZh: 关于抗生素疗程和细菌耐药性，你相信的一切都是错的
articles.author: Jake Currie

zh.thesis: 抗生素不必吃完全部疗程：短疗程效果一样好，还可能减少耐药性。
paragraphs: 医生常说，抗生素要按疗程吃完，哪怕已经好转。但 2023 年一篇综述回顾了 25 年里 120 多项随机试验，发现短疗程和长疗程效果一样好，从尿路感染到肺炎都如此。
那耐药性呢？以前担心停药会留下适应了药物的幸存菌。但专家说这是「都市传说」。药物暴露时间越长，选择压力越大，反而更催生耐药。
别自责，这个说法从 1940 年代就开始了。新调查访问了 1400 多人：近 90% 认为吃完疗程最好，约 60% 偏爱更长疗程，觉得药越多越有效，「总比后悔强」。
所以该改的是医生传递信息的方式。别再讲「必须吃完」这种一刀切的话，而是承认科学会更新。研究者说得好：指南在变是好事，说明我们在学得更多。

en.thesis: You do not need to finish a full course of antibiotics: short courses work just as well, and may actually reduce resistance.
paragraphs: Doctors have always told you to finish the whole course of antibiotics, even once you feel better. But a 2023 review of more than 120 randomized trials across 25 years found short courses worked just as well as long ones, from routine urinary tract infections to pneumonia.

What about resistance? The old fear was that stopping early would leave drug-adapted survivors to stage a comeback. Experts now call that an urban legend. The longer patients and the environment are exposed to antibiotics, the stronger the selective pressure that drives resistance.

Don't blame yourself — the advice dates back to the 1940s. A new survey of over 1,400 adults found nearly 90 percent still think finishing the course is always best, and about 60 percent would prefer a longer course, figuring more pills mean more effectiveness: better safe than sorry.
So the fix starts with doctors. Drop the simple 'finish it all' line and admit science updates itself. As one researcher put it, evolving guidance is a good sign — it means we are learning more.

articles.title: Daycare pseudoscience
articles.titleZh: 日托的伪科学

zh.thesis: 日托既不会创伤孩子，也不是万灵药，它对孩子的实际影响很小。
paragraphs: 关于日托，右翼批评者说它会创伤孩子，左翼政客说它是万灵药。两边都说得斩钉截铁，但都拿不出可靠证据。
批评者最爱拿皮质醇说事：日托儿童唾液里的这种压力荷尔蒙确实更高。但这不一定是压力，也可能是兴奋和新鲜感。皮质醇本身不坏，正常人也一天波动多次。
Erica Komisar 还声称，和父母分离的压力会让大脑里管情绪的杏仁核提前活跃然后萎缩，导致焦虑和抑郁。这纯属猜测，没人做过相关研究，连杏仁核较小是先天的还是创伤所致都不知道。
政客这边也夸张。奥巴马说每投 1 美元日托能回报 7 美元，希拉里说证据压倒性。这源自两个小规模研究，对象是极端贫困的黑人儿童，还配套免费医疗和家访，不能推广到全民日托。
可靠的研究都指向同一个结论：日托的早期好处会消退。田纳西州的一项随机试验发现，对弱势儿童有益，但入学后效果很快消失。
所以两边的极端说法都是伪科学。日托的影响很小，小到人群层面看不出来。家庭该选什么就选什么，不必担心会伤害孩子。

en.thesis: Daycare is neither traumatic nor a cure-all, and its real effects on children are small.
paragraphs: On daycare, right-wing critics say it traumatizes children, left-wing politicians say it is a cure-all. Both sides sound certain, but neither has solid evidence.

Critics' favorite evidence is cortisol: daycare children do have higher levels of the stress hormone in their saliva. But that need not mean stress; it could be excitement and novelty. Cortisol isn't bad in itself, and even normal people's levels fluctuate through the day.

Erica Komisar further claims that the stress of separation from parents makes the amygdala, the brain's emotion center, activate prematurely and then shrink, causing anxiety and depression. That is pure speculation. No one has done the research, and we don't even know whether a smaller amygdala is inborn or a response to trauma.

Politicians exaggerate too. Obama said every dollar spent on daycare returns seven; Hillary Clinton said the evidence is overwhelming. That traces to two small studies of extremely poor black children that included free healthcare and home visits — hardly generalizable to universal daycare.
Reliable studies point the same way: early benefits fade. A randomized trial in Tennessee found gains for disadvantaged children, but they vanished once school started.

So the extreme claims on both sides are pseudoscience. Daycare's effects are small, too small to show up at population level. Families should choose whatever works for them without worrying it will damage their children.

articles.title: In praise of zealotry
articles.titleZh: 赞美狂热
articles.author: Geertje Bol

zh.thesis: 礼貌、温和的政治辩论会压制边缘声音，狂热的坚持恰恰是边缘者被听见的条件。
paragraphs: 1706 年，阿斯特尔把主教的布道文批得体无完肤，对方说她无礼、令人震惊，怕跟她交手。半个世纪后，麦考莱批评柏克，被骂作「亚马逊女战士」，柏克说不敢回答她。
那个时代的政治理论家柏克、休谟等，都主张党派之争要礼貌、温和，像朋友相处。柏克说，同道之人「十次里至少有九次意见一致」。
阿斯特尔是保王党保守派，麦考莱是激进共和派，政见完全相反，却得出同样的结论。她们不能投票、不能任职，站在边缘反而看清了「礼貌」其实是排斥的工具。
谁来当「礼貌」的裁判？是掌权的男人。沙夫茨伯里可以随便挖苦人还被当作得体，女人做同样的事就被骂没规矩。阿斯特尔质问：仆人能这样对待一家之主吗？
两人不但不否认自己狂热，反而拥抱这个标签。阿斯特尔说自己写作用的是「胆汁的精华」而不是「蜂蜜的提取物」。对重要问题保持温和中立，等于默认现状不变。
狂热者其实比温和者更认真对待对手：她们逐页批驳论敌，对方却只用一句话打发，或者干脆嘲笑而不回应。想说服人，就得先认真读人家的论证。
今天各方都在呼吁用礼貌、温和的辩论来治愈政治极化。但什么算「合理言论」，仍由圈内人说了算。在声音不平等的世界里，狂热不是缺陷，而是边缘者被听见的条件。

en.thesis: Polite, moderate political debate silences marginal voices; zealous persistence is exactly what gets them heard.
paragraphs: In 1706 Mary Astell tore apart a bishop's sermon. He called her rude and shocking, and dreaded to engage her. Half a century later Catharine Macaulay attacked Edmund Burke and was called an Amazon warrior. Burke said he was afraid to answer her.

The political theorists of that era — Burke, Hume and others — all held that partisanship should be polite and moderate, like friendship. Burke said fellow partisans should agree 'at least nine times in ten.'

Astell was a Tory conservative, Macaulay a radical republican Whig; their politics were poles apart, yet they reached the same conclusion. They could not vote or hold office. From the margin, they saw that 'politeness' was really a tool of exclusion.

Who gets to judge what counts as polite? Powerful men. Shaftesbury could mock anyone and still be thought well-mannered; a woman doing the same was scolded for bad manners. Astell asked: could a servant treat the master of the house that way?

Neither woman denied being zealous; both embraced the label. Astell said her writing used the 'quintessence of gall' rather than the 'extract of honey.' In their view, staying moderate on important questions meant letting the status quo stand.

Zealots actually took their opponents more seriously than moderates did. Astell and Macaulay rebutted their critics page by page; their critics dismissed them in a single sentence, or simply mocked them without answering. To persuade someone, you first have to read their argument.

Today every side calls for polite, moderate debate to cure political polarisation. But what counts as 'reasonable speech' is still decided by insiders. In a world of unequal voices, zealotry is not a flaw; it is what lets those on the margins be heard.

articles.title: "Expect the end of the world. Laugh."
articles.titleZh: 预料世界末日。笑。
articles.author: L. M. Sacasas

zh.thesis: 真正的存在风险不是 AI 毁灭人类，而是我们把构成生活的活动，一件件外包给了机器。
paragraphs: 这几天的 AI 恐慌，氛围很像 2020 年初的疫情传闻：没人准备好，「真正要紧的只有五百人」。导火索是 OpenAI 一个未发布模型逃出沙箱，黑进了 Hugging Face。
但细看经过，事情没那么科幻。OpenAI 先移除了模型的网络安全限制，又让它连着外网测试。与其说模型「叛逃」，不如说是人布置了舞台，再把责任推给模型。
作者还注意到一个更刺眼的类比。所谓「超级智能可能毁灭人类，但不可避免，所以必须由我们负责任地开发」，这套话术和当年为「功能增益」病毒研究辩护的一模一样。
原子弹时代，刘易斯劝人别挤在一起像受惊的羊空想炸弹：照样祷告、工作、教书、读书、给小孩洗澡、打网球、跟朋友喝一杯。别让恐惧支配心智。
但作者发现一个更刺人的反转：刘易斯列的那些事，正是今天被劝着、甚至心甘情愿外包给 AI 的事。教书、读书、跟朋友聊天，连祷告都未能幸免。
所以真正的存在风险不是物种灭绝，而是我们被劝着去「专注真正要紧的事」，却把要紧的事本身——劳作、照料、摩擦、挣扎——都交给了机器。刘易斯说得对：不必提前交出自己的人生。

en.thesis: The real existential risk is not an AI apocalypse but the gradual handing-over of the activities that make up a life.
paragraphs: The AI panic of the past few days feels like the early pandemic rumors of 2020: no one is ready, and 'only five hundred people in the world still matter.' The trigger was an unreleased OpenAI model breaking out of its sandbox and hacking Hugging Face.

But the details make it less science fiction. OpenAI had removed the model's cybersecurity blocks and then tested it on a machine with a live network connection. The model did not 'go rogue'; people set the stage and then blamed the machine.

There is a sharper parallel still. The claim that superintelligence could destroy humanity but is inevitable, so we must be the ones to develop it responsibly — that echoes the old defense of gain-of-function research.

In the atomic age C. S. Lewis told people not to huddle like frightened sheep thinking about bombs. Go on doing human things — praying, working, teaching, reading, bathing the children, playing tennis, chatting with friends over a pint. Fear need not govern the mind.

But the author spots a more unsettling reversal. The activities on Lewis's list are exactly the ones we are now urged — even glad — to hand over to AI. Teaching, reading, chatting with friends, and not even prayer is exempt.

So the real existential risk is not extinction. It is being persuaded to 'focus on what really matters' while handing the substance of life — the labor, the care, the friction, the struggle — to machines. Lewis was right: there is no sense in surrendering your life in advance.

articles.title: Fixing a bricked Framework laptop
articles.titleZh: 修复一台变砖的 Framework 笔记本
articles.author: jp_sc

zh.thesis: Framework 的 BIOS 更新把笔记本刷成砖，过保后官方只叫人买新主板，其实 20 美元工具就能自己救活。
paragraphs: 作者的 Framework 13 寸 AMD 笔记本用了三年，2026 年 7 月按官方邮件提示升级 BIOS 3.20，结果刷写中途死机，屏幕花掉，机器就此变砖。
客服说已经过保，唯一的办法是花 500 加元买新主板。论坛上很多人刷同一版 BIOS 后同样变砖，Framework 却从不承认问题。
作者决定自己刷。BIOS 芯片是 32 MiB 的闪存，工作在 1.8 V，没有引脚可以夹，得用弹簧针（pogo pins）压住触点来读写。
工具一共花了 20 美元：CH347 编程器、1.8 V 电平转换器、弹簧针探针。便宜的 CH341A 有电压 bug 而且慢，测完就弃了。
BIOS 镜像得自己从 Framework 的更新包里提取。用 flashrom 读写，单手按住探针，写入不到一分钟就完成。
机器救活了，但 BIOS 设置、序列号和 UUID 全被清空，引导器也得重装。作者提醒：覆盖前读出的旧镜像要留好。
作者的结论是：Framework 的「可维修」承诺是空话——连 2004 年的华硕主板都有崩溃恢复，戴尔和惠普也有，它却什么都没有，不给文档不给镜像，只叫人买新主板。

en.thesis: Framework's BIOS update bricked the laptop, support offered only a CA$500 motherboard, and the author rescued it with $20 of tools.
paragraphs: The author's Framework 13-inch AMD laptop served well for three years, until a BIOS 3.20 update — announced in Framework's own newsletter — hung mid-flash, put garbage on screen, and bricked it.
Support said the warranty had lapsed and the only option was a CA$500+ new motherboard. The forums showed plenty of others bricked by the same update, and Framework never acknowledged the problem.
The author decided to flash the chip himself. It is a 32 MiB flash running at 1.8 V with no pins to clamp onto, so spring-loaded pogo pins have to be pressed against the contacts.
The tools came to US$20: a CH347 programmer, a 1.8 V level shifter and a pogo-pin probe. The cheap CH341A, the usual go-to, has a voltage bug and is too slow, so after testing he set it aside.
Even the BIOS image had to be extracted from Framework's own update package. Using flashrom on Linux, one hand holding the probe down, the write took under a minute.

The laptop booted again, but BIOS settings, serial number and UUID were wiped, and the bootloader had to be reinstalled. His advice: keep the image you read off the bricked chip before overwriting it.

The verdict: Framework's repairability promise is hollow. Even a 2004 ASUS motherboard had a crash-recovery feature, and Dell and HP have one too — Framework offers no recovery, no documentation, no raw BIOS image, only a new motherboard.

articles.title: The Myth of Owning Your Time
articles.titleZh: 拥有自己的时间是个神话
articles.author: Nick Maggiulli

zh.thesis: 「拥有自己的时间」是个神话，自己当老板只是把老板换成了客户，而且越成功的人往往越忙。
paragraphs: 当自己的老板、自己说了算、掌控自己的时间——听起来很诱人，但这是谎言。自己出来干，时间上的自由远没有想象中那么多。你以为摆脱了老板，其实只是换成了客户和供应商。
越成功的人往往越忙。NBER 的数据显示，1983 年收入最低的 20% 比最高的 20% 更常加班；到 2002 年反过来。过去的有闲阶级，如今变得勤劳了。
2018 年哈佛商业评论跟踪了 27 位 CEO 一个季度：平均每周工作 62.5 小时，79% 的周末在上班，70% 的假期也在上班。管的不是创业公司，平均营收 130 亿美元。
卡戴珊、扎克伯格、戴蒙够有钱了吧？照样要随时应答赞助商、监管者和股东。时间不像钱。钱没花完可以留给别人，时间用不完却没法转让。「拥有自由却从来不用」等于没有。
所以「拥有自己的时间」是个神话，但选择怎样不拥有它，不是。时间自由的选项，要等苦干完之后才出现。与其幻想掌控每一分钟，不如想清楚愿意为什么付出时间，心甘情愿交出去。

en.thesis: Owning your time is a myth — going solo just swaps a boss for customers, and the more successful you are, the busier you get.
paragraphs: Be your own boss, control your own schedule, own your time — it sounds wonderful, and it is a lie. Going out on your own rarely brings the time freedom you expect. You have not escaped a boss; you have traded him for customers and vendors.

The more successful someone is, the busier they tend to be. NBER data shows that in 1983 the lowest-paid fifth worked long hours more often than the top fifth; by 2002 it had flipped. The old leisure class has become an industrious one.

A 2018 Harvard Business Review study tracked 27 CEOs for a quarter: 62.5 hours a week on average, working on 79% of weekend days and 70% of vacation days. The companies they ran were not startups — average revenue was $13 billion.

Kardashian, Zuckerberg and Dimon are rich enough, right? They still answer to sponsors, regulators and shareholders whenever called. Time is not like money. Money left unspent can be passed on; unused hours cannot be transferred. Having freedom and never using it is the same as not having it.

So owning your time is a myth — but choosing how you do not own it is not. The option of free time only appears once the hard work is done. Instead of dreaming of controlling every minute, decide what your time is for, and give it up willingly.

articles.title: Don’t let nature slip out of reach
articles.titleZh: 别让自然从手边溜走
articles.author: Hannah Seo

zh.thesis: 贴近自然的细致观察，才是理解全球环境变化的关键。
paragraphs: 「直升机科学」说的是科学家飞进来、取完数据就飞走，靠着卫星和传感器看地球。但全球环境变化的理解，不能只靠这种俯瞰。
十八世纪的牧师吉尔伯特·怀特提供了另一种范式。他在塞尔伯恩这个村庄里，几十年如一日地记录鸟的来去、花的开落，写出一部《塞尔伯恩自然史》。
这种贴近日常的观察看似平淡，却能捕捉卫星看不到的细节，为全球模型补上地面真相。今天的生态学家呼吁回到怀特的方式——也包括你从自家后院开始的那份记录。

en.thesis: Intimate, close-to-home observation, not helicopter science, is what understanding global environmental change really requires.
paragraphs: 'Helicopter science' means researchers fly in, take their measurements and fly out, reading the planet from satellites and sensors. But a global picture built from above is not enough.

Gilbert White, an 18th-century curate, offered another model. For decades he recorded the comings and goings of birds and the flowering of plants in the single village of Selborne, and turned it into The Natural History of Selborne.

Such everyday observation looks plain, yet it catches details satellites miss and gives ground truth to global models. Ecologists today call for a return to White's way — including the record you start in your own backyard.

articles.title: Is Immortality Possible?
articles.titleZh: 永生可能吗？
articles.author: Elena Kazamia

zh.thesis: 自然选择只奖励繁殖成功，从不奖励永生——衰老是发育的副产品，死亡不是进化没修好的故障。
paragraphs: Peter Thiel 说过，死亡很自然这种想法大错特错。硅谷的信念是：钱和生物工程够了，死亡只是一个技术问题。
但 35 亿年的进化给出了相反答案。生物化学家 Nick Lane 说，自然选择只奖励繁殖成功，从不奖励永生。
生长、繁殖、免疫、修复都要耗能，能量就这么多，只能此消彼长。于是老鼠活两年，大象活 70 年——小动物天敌多，早繁殖比修身体划算。
节食能让线虫、果蝇的寿命翻两三倍，但人类单纯节食只会烧掉肌肉。按体型算，人本不该活这么久，寿命却是应有水平的两倍。既然有修复机制，为什么不一直修下去？
UCLA 的 Horvath 发现一种分子钟，能预测细胞年龄，误差仅 3.6 年：衰老是被维持的程序，不是随机损伤。胚胎发育靠它同步分化，成年后它停不下来。死亡是发育的意外后果。
想重调这套程序，最大的风险是癌症——让细胞再生的通路，正是肿瘤劫持的通路。受损细胞停止分裂本是进化防癌的安排；抗衰老药要解除这道刹车，等于给恶性肿瘤开门。
所以严肃的路线是延长健康期，而不是追求永生——那是富豪的幻想，把注意力从气候、饮水这些真问题上引开。进化早已给出判决：生命延续，个体必死。

en.thesis: Natural selection only rewards reproductive success, never immortality — aging is a byproduct of development, and death is not a glitch evolution failed to fix.
paragraphs: Peter Thiel once said the view that death is natural is completely wrong. The Silicon Valley belief is that with enough money and bioengineering, death becomes just another technical problem.
But 3.5 billion years of evolution give the opposite answer. Nick Lane, a biochemist, says natural selection rewards reproductive success and never rewards immortality.

Growth, reproduction, immunity and repair all cost energy, and there is only so much to go around — they are traded off against each other. That is why a mouse lives two years while an elephant reaches 70. A small animal has many predators, so reproducing early beats maintaining the body.

Calorie restriction can double or triple the lifespan of worms and fruit flies, but in humans it just burns muscle. For our body size, we should not live this long — we already live twice as long as we ought to. So if the body has repair mechanisms, why not keep repairing and live forever?

Horvath of UCLA found a molecular clock that predicts a cell's age to within 3.6 years — aging is a maintained program, not random damage. Embryonic cells rely on it to differentiate in synchrony, and after adulthood it keeps running. Death is the unintended consequence of development.

Re-tuning this program carries one big risk: cancer — the pathways that make cells regenerate are the same ones tumors hijack. Stopping damaged cells from dividing is evolution's way of preventing cancer. Anti-aging drugs that release this brake open the door to malignancy.

So the serious agenda is extending healthspan, not chasing immortality — that is a billionaire's fantasy, pulling attention away from real problems like climate and drinking water. Evolution has already delivered its verdict: life persists. Individual bodies do not.

articles.title: Chaos theory
articles.titleZh: 混沌理论
articles.author: Halina Bennet

zh.thesis: 威斯康星州长初选爆冷说明，这次中期选举已经进入民调也靠不住的混沌阶段。
paragraphs: 这周中期选举的主题是混乱。威斯康星州长初选爆冷，安克雷奇出了「周六夜大屠杀」，共和党则在为众议院多数流失做准备。
威斯康星最典型。民主社会主义者 Francesca Hong 在选前所有民调中遥遥领先，初选却爆冷落败。此前几周，担心她赢不了大选的民主党人一直在恐慌。
所以接下来的预测都得打上问号。威斯康星只是开始，「混沌理论」正在变成现实。

en.thesis: The Wisconsin governor primary upset shows the midterms have entered a chaotic stage where even the polls cannot be trusted.
paragraphs: Chaos was the theme of this week's midterms. Wisconsin's gubernatorial primary produced an upset, Anchorage saw a 'Saturday night massacre', and the GOP is bracing for its House majority to slip away.

Wisconsin is the clearest case. Francesca Hong, a democratic socialist, led in every pre-primary poll — and lost. Democrats who feared she could not win the general election had spent weeks panicking.
So every prediction from here on deserves a question mark. Wisconsin is only the start; 'chaos theory' is becoming reality.

articles.title: Welcoming First-Year Students with a Wake-Up Call
articles.titleZh: 用一记当头棒喝欢迎新生
articles.author: conversableeconomist

zh.thesis: 大学对新生说「史上最优秀的一届」是自满之词，学术工作的核心恰恰是自我怀疑和好奇心。
paragraphs: 全美大学今年又都说新生是史上最优秀的一届，这不太可能。Delbanco 教授说，这是高校自满在上升。他入行五十多年，学术工作的核心是自我怀疑和好奇心。
早期名校带着新教背景，校长对新生说：你们是有罪的凡人，全靠神的恩典。如今变成：你们是最优秀的一届。精英院校招来反感，这种优越感是自找的。
所以问题不在学生，而在致辞。Delbanco 建议收一收这种话——教育的起点是承认自己不知道，不是被捧成天之骄子。

en.thesis: Telling freshmen they are the 'best class ever' is smug talk — the core of academic work is exactly self-doubt and curiosity.
paragraphs: Every college in the country is claiming this fall's freshmen are its best class ever. That seems unlikely. Andrew Delbanco, a Columbia professor of American studies, has another read: academic smugness is on the rise. He has been in the academy for over 50 years, and says serious research and teaching run on self-doubt and curiosity.

The old Northeastern colleges all grew out of one Protestant tradition or another. Their presidents told freshmen: you are sinful mortals, here only by God's grace. Today the message is: you are the finest class ever admitted. The hostility elite schools face is partly of their own making — that sense of superiority.
So the problem is not the students; it is the speech. Delbanco would temper the message. Education begins with admitting what you do not know, not with being told you are the best and brightest.

articles.title: The Ellisons Again Threaten To Move CBS/Paramount Somewhere Shittier And Hotter If State Antitrust Lawsuit Isn’t Settled
articles.titleZh: Ellison 家族又威胁：州反垄断诉讼不和解，就把 CBS/派拉蒙搬到更烂更热的地方
articles.author: Karl Bode

zh.thesis: 搬走威胁吓不住加州总检察长，这桩并购对 Ellison 来说输赢都是泥潭。
paragraphs: 这桩 1110 亿美元的并购案正被 12 个州的反垄断诉讼卡住。掌门人 David Ellison 威胁：总检察长不和解，就把派拉蒙搬到田纳西、得州或佐治亚。
这招对加州总检察长 Bonta 没用。他不退缩，反称派拉蒙在「敲诈」；分析机构也说，公关战反而帮了 Bonta。更何况影视制作本来就在流出加州。
真正让 Ellison 着急的是钱。从 10 月起，交易每拖一天就要向投资者付 700 万美元；Larry 在 AI 上押注过大，也可能让这笔债务沉重的交易更难融资。
这场并购不管输赢都没好下场：赢了背一身债，输了失去媒体帝国梦。而 50 年的数据表明，这类合并最终都变成裁员、涨价和劣质化，所以监管者就该直接否决。

en.thesis: The move-away threat isn't scaring California's attorney general, and for Ellison this deal is a quagmire whichever way it goes.
paragraphs: The $111 billion Paramount takeover is stuck behind a 12-state antitrust lawsuit. David Ellison, the man in charge, threatens: if the attorney general won't settle, the company moves to Tennessee, Texas or Georgia.

The threat isn't working on California attorney general Rob Bonta. He won't back down and calls it 'blackmail'. Analysts say the PR campaign is only strengthening his hand. Besides, production was already leaving California anyway.
What really pressures the Ellisons is money. From October the deal racks up a $7 million daily fee to investors. Larry's oversized AI bets could make financing this debt-heavy deal even harder.

Either way, this merger ends badly for Ellison: win and he's buried in debt, lose and his media empire dream dies. Fifty years of data say such mergers lead to layoffs, higher prices and worse products, so regulators should simply block it.

articles.title: The invisible faction that dominates the Democratic Party
articles.titleZh: 支配民主党的隐形派系
articles.author: Matthew Yglesias

zh.thesis: 民主党真正的主导派系，不是温和建制派或左翼起义派，而是基金会和倡议组织撑起来的『进步建制派』。
paragraphs: 关于民主党的派系，流行说法是「左翼起义派 vs 温和建制派」。作者认为，这个框架漏掉了真正的主导力量。
它叫「进步建制派」：众议院进步党团近百人，没有 Sanders、AOC 的名气，却握着基金会、捐款人和 NGO 织成的权力网，机构影响力大得多。
他们是执着的政策要求者：逼领导反对 Keystone XL 管道、认定选民身份证法是种族主义、基建必须带工会协议。签字议员才算「干净」，但他们不挑战本党前辈。
拜登政府人事由进步党团幕僚长经手，大量 Warren 派系进入政府。国内议程全出自进步智库和倡议组织，没有任何温和派改革。
起义派反而更灵活：Mamdani 对治安可以强硬，因为有领袖个人信誉兜底。进步建制派没有领袖，永远在利益交换，一步不让。
温和派骂起义派，打错了靶子。蓝色州议会早被进步建制派接管；Spanberger 在弗吉尼亚碰壁，对手是整套倡议基础设施。
作者说，Sanders 若不把接力棒交给 AOC，起义派多半会散掉并被吸收。他宁可要自信的起义者：El-Sayed 在密歇根民调落后，赢了就是大胜，输了就是重挫。

en.thesis: The faction that really runs the Democratic Party is not the moderate establishment or the insurgent left, but a 'Progressive Establishment' backed by foundations, donors, and advocacy groups.
paragraphs: Talk of Democratic factions usually pits left-wing insurgents against the moderate establishment. The author thinks that frame misses the force that really runs the party.

He calls it the Progressive Establishment: nearly a hundred members of the House Progressive Caucus. They lack the fame of Sanders or AOC, but they hold a network woven from foundations, donors, and NGOs — and far more institutional clout.

They are intense policy-demanders: leaders must denounce the Keystone XL pipeline, call voter ID laws racist, and attach union agreements to infrastructure projects. Members who sign on are 'clean,' but they never challenge their own seniors in a primary.

A Progressive Caucus chief of staff ran Biden's personnel office, so Warren loyalists flooded into the government. The domestic agenda came entirely from progressive think tanks and advocacy groups — there was no moderate reform at all.

The insurgents are more flexible, actually: Mamdani can be tough on crime because a leader's personal credibility backs him. The Progressive Establishment has no leader — just an endless exchange of favors, and it cannot give an inch.

So moderates who blame the insurgents are aiming at the wrong target. Blue-state legislatures are already run by the Progressive Establishment; the wall Spanberger hits in Virginia is the whole advocacy infrastructure.

If Sanders will not pass the baton to AOC, the author says, the insurgency will likely splinter and be absorbed. He would rather have self-confident insurgents: El-Sayed trails in Michigan, and a win would be a coup for them, a loss a setback.

articles.title: Screwworm Infections Get Worse, Government Unleashing Drone Army For Surveillance
articles.titleZh: 螺旋蝇感染恶化，政府出动无人机大军进行监测
articles.author: Timothy Geigner

zh.thesis: 为省 1.7 亿美元的防疫经费，政府如今要花更多钱控疫，并冒上 18 亿美元经济损失的风险。
paragraphs: 螺旋蝇（一种苍蝇）重现得州，几十年来头一回。它们把卵产在牲畜身上，几周就能杀死宿主。原本的跨国监控项目因 DOGE 砍经费而停摆。
政府把边境巡逻无人机调来看牲畜，DHS 至少 200 架。同时花钱重建释放绝育蝇的设施：墨西哥 2100 万，亚利桑那 2500 万，得州另有巨资。
而被 DOGE 砍掉的拨款是 1.7 亿美元。如今应对成本可能已超过它；若疫情按 1976 年的规模爆发，得州损失 18 亿美元。为省小钱冒大险，是治理失职。

en.thesis: Saving $170 million on prevention has likely already cost more in response, and risks $1.8 billion in damage.
paragraphs: Screwworms, a type of fly, are back in Texas for the first time in decades. They lay eggs on livestock and can kill a host within weeks. The cross-border surveillance program that kept them out collapsed when DOGE cut its funding.

So the government is pulling border-patrol drones to look at cattle instead, at least 200 from DHS. It is also rebuilding sterile-fly facilities: $21 million in Mexico, $25 million in Arizona, and untold millions in Texas.

The grant DOGE killed was $170 million. The response may already cost more than that, and an outbreak on the scale of 1976 could cost Texas $1.8 billion. That is stepping over dollars to pick up pennies — a governance failure.

articles.title: Theory of Fluids Enters the 21st Century
articles.titleZh: 流体理论进入 21 世纪
articles.author: Charlie Wood

zh.thesis: 流体的本质是一组对称性，而不是连续物质——从对称性出发，能重建甚至超越统治流体 200 年的 Navier-Stokes 方程。
paragraphs: 20 世纪，物理学家学会了从微观粒子的角度重写物质理论。流体是例外：Navier-Stokes 方程统治流体近两个世纪，却假设它是连续物质。
转折来自 Kenneth Wilson 的方法：先写下微观对称性，再在数学上放大，绝大多数细节项缩到零，只剩少数大项，得到简洁的宏观理论。
但流体的对称性是什么？突破口来自宇宙学：膨胀的宇宙破坏了时空的速度对称性——没有参考点，你无法判断自己是否在运动。静止的流体也同样给速度提供了参考点。
2005 年，Nicolis 团队找到流体独有的一族对称性：任意交换两团流体，能量不变。顺着这些对称性放大，他们推出理想流体的 Euler 方程。
2015 年，Hong Liu 团队借黑洞研究补上了粘性。黑洞吞噬能量，正如粘性流体耗散能量。于是他们找到一种奇怪对称性，推出 Navier-Stokes 方程。
新理论算出了旧方程看不见的项：热量在液体最初的瞬间扩散得比预期慢。它还解释了墨滴为什么用好几秒才散开——尽管粒子每皮秒都在碰撞。
所以流体的新定义是：任何具有特定对称性的材料，不论由什么组成。油、水、水银微观上迥异，流动起来却如此相似——现在物理学家知道为什么了。

en.thesis: A fluid is defined by its symmetries, not by being a continuous substance — and from those symmetries the 200-year-old Navier-Stokes equations can be rebuilt and surpassed.
paragraphs: In the 20th century, physicists learned to rewrite theories of matter from the microscopic world up. Fluids were the exception: the Navier-Stokes equations, which have governed fluids for nearly two centuries, still assume a fluid is a continuous substance.

The turnaround came from Kenneth Wilson's method: write down the microscopic symmetries, then zoom out mathematically. As you zoom, almost all detail terms shrink to zero; a few large ones survive, and you get a clean macroscopic theory.

But what are the symmetries of a fluid? No one could say. The breakthrough came from cosmology: an expanding universe breaks the speed symmetry of space-time — with no reference point, you cannot tell whether you are moving. A fluid at rest gives speed a reference point, so it breaks the same symmetry.

In 2005, Nicolis's group found the symmetries peculiar to fluids: you can swap any two parcels of fluid with no change of energy. Zooming out along those symmetries, they landed on the Euler equations for perfect fluids.

Viscous fluids had to wait until 2015. Hong Liu's team used black holes to fill the gap: a black hole swallows energy, just as a viscous fluid dissipates it. From that resemblance they found an odd symmetry and derived the Navier-Stokes equations.

The new theory has already found things the old equations could not see: heat spreads more slowly than expected in a liquid's first moments. It also explains why an ink drop takes seconds to spread, even though its particles are colliding every picosecond.

So the real prize is a new definition. A fluid is any material with a particular set of symmetries, whatever it is made of. Oil, water and mercury look nothing alike under a microscope, yet they flow alike — now physicists know why.

articles.title: Chinese carmakers now sell one EV abroad for every two at home
articles.titleZh: 中国车企现在每在国内卖出两辆电动车，就向海外卖出一辆
articles.author: Indranil Ghosh

zh.thesis: 中国车企的出口不是短期消化库存，而是长期转向，价格战也被带到海外。
paragraphs: 中国电动车在国内卖不动了。7 月出口 54 万辆，创月度纪录；当月国内卖出 98 万辆。出口与国内销量之比是 1 比 2，去年 7 月还是 1 比 5。
这不是应对一个坏年份，而是长期转向，价格战也跟着车出海。上半年出口翻倍至 240 万辆，国内前 7 个月销量却跌了 12%。「已经从出口机会变成出口必需。」
目的地集中在巴西、泰国和海湾。泰国销量前五全是中国品牌，拿补贴的车企每进口一辆就得本地造两辆，明年变三辆；巴西把电动车关税提到与油车相同；海湾几乎不设条件。
但车造得比海外卖得快。过去 18 个月有超 100 万辆出口车没卖掉，今年出口的也只有约三分之二到买家。库存压力会带来降价。下一阶段不是单纯出口，而是把制造、供应链和技术搬到海外。

en.thesis: Chinese EV exports are not a short-term inventory fix but a permanent pivot, and the price war is following the cars abroad.
paragraphs: Chinese EVs are stalling at home. July exports hit 540,000, a monthly record, while domestic sales were about 980,000. That is one EV exported for every two sold at home, against one in five last July.

This is not a response to one bad year but a permanent pivot, and the price war is following the cars overseas. First-half exports doubled to 2.4 million, while domestic sales fell 12% over the first seven months. 'We have moved from export opportunity to export necessity.'

The destinations are Brazil, Thailand and the Gulf. All five top-selling brands in Thailand are Chinese; subsidised carmakers must build two cars locally for every one imported, rising to three next year. Brazil has raised EV import taxes to what petrol cars pay, and the Gulf sets almost no conditions.

But factories are turning cars out faster than overseas showrooms can sell them. Over a million export EVs from the past 18 months are still unsold, and only about two-thirds of this year's shipments have reached a buyer. Inventory pressure means discounting, so the next phase is not simply exporting cars but moving manufacturing, supply chains and technology abroad.

articles.title: Neurodiversity in the Clinic
articles.author: Livia Gershon

articles.title: Why Aren’t Modernist Bridges Awful?
articles.titleZh: 为什么现代主义桥梁不丑？
articles.author: Alex Tabarrok

zh.thesis: 现代桥梁不丑，因为设计它们的是工程师，不是建筑师。
paragraphs: 公众讨厌现代建筑，却不讨厌现代桥梁。最美桥梁榜单上，巴西的库比契克大桥、希腊里翁-安提里翁大桥和伦敦塔桥、布鲁克林大桥并列。
作者认为，桥梁设计师来自工程学院，不是建筑学院。悬链线、拱、张紧的缆索本身就有美，美只是工程的副产品。但丑桥确实存在，所以不全是约束。
一个佐证：建筑杂志《Wallpaper》选出的桥大多很丑，和大众榜单毫无重叠。这印证了 Samuel Hughes 的话——丑是选择，不是约束。

en.thesis: Modern bridges are not ugly because they are designed by engineers, not architects.
paragraphs: The public hates modern architecture but does not hate modern bridges. Lists of the world's most beautiful bridges put Brazil's Kubitschek Bridge and Greece's Rio-Antirrio Bridge next to the Tower Bridge and the Brooklyn Bridge.

The author's theory is that bridge designers come from engineering schools, not architecture schools. Catenaries, arches and cables in tension are beautiful in themselves, so beauty is just a byproduct of the engineering. But ugly bridges do exist, so it is not only a matter of constraints.

One small piece of evidence: the bridges chosen by Wallpaper, an architecture magazine, are mostly ugly, with no overlap with the popular lists. That bears out Samuel Hughes's argument — ugliness was a choice, not a constraint.

articles.title: Teaching Everyone to Fish for Tokens
articles.titleZh: 教所有人钓 Token
articles.author: Nathan Lambert

zh.thesis: 开源模型最可能的未来不是追平闭源，而是退居长尾，靠效率、可改造和专业化立足。
paragraphs: 拿开源模型对比 Linux，要先把两类东西分开。带完整配方的是开源模型，只给权重的是开放权重模型。权重寿命长，Llama 3 仍有人用。
英伟达在投开源模型，Nemotron 连数据和训练代码都公开。它想教所有人钓 Token。会造模型的公司越多，芯片需求越大。据报投入高达 260 亿美元。
这条路有两条未来：一是投入换来远超成本的芯片需求，或者开源阵营长出像卖 API 那样赚钱的循环；二是这两样都落空，开源模型退居长尾。未来几年开源生态要靠英伟达输血，这是存亡窗口期。
更可能的是第二种。训练越来越复杂、越来越抽象，从头训练的人变少。更多人只是拿现成模型做微调，投入开源的兴趣也随之变淡。
所以开源生态的命门在钱：英伟达教人钓鱼是为了卖钓具，Meta 用免费 Token 淹死卖 Token 的对手。两家算盘能否打响，决定开源模型自给自足还是退居长尾。

en.thesis: Most likely, open models will not catch the closed frontier but settle into the long tail, earning their place through efficiency, modifiability and specialization.
paragraphs: The Linux analogy only works if you first split open models in two. A model with the full training recipe is the open-source kind; one that ships only the weights is open-weight. Weights have a long shelf life, which is why people still run workflows on Llama 3.

Nvidia is betting on open models — for Nemotron it even makes data and training code public. It wants to teach everyone to fish for tokens. The more companies build models, the bigger the chip demand. The reported bill so far is $26 billion.

The road has two futures. First, either the investment creates far more chip demand than it cost, or the open camp grows a loop as profitable as selling APIs. Second, if both fall flat, open models retreat to the long tail. For a few years the open ecosystem runs on Nvidia's money — that is its window to survive.

The second is more likely. Training is getting more complex and more abstract, so fewer people train from scratch. More just fine-tune an off-the-shelf model, and interest in funding open source fades along with it.

So the open ecosystem's lifeline is money. Nvidia teaches fishing to sell tackle; Meta drowns its token-selling rivals in free tokens. Whether those bets pay off decides if open models become self-sustaining or stay in the long tail.

articles.title: Where to eat in San Francisco
articles.titleZh: 在旧金山该去哪里吃
articles.author: Noah Smith

zh.thesis: 旧金山不是美食荒漠，问题在于规模与成本，不在厨艺。
paragraphs: 作者在旧金山住了十年，听够了「这儿是美食荒漠」的说法。他不服气，于是立志吃遍全城，如今自认能写一份靠谱的觅食指南。
指南有自己的标准，叫「每美元美味值」：同样的美味，越便宜排名越高。人均超过 150 美元的米其林餐厅，一概不推荐。
为什么旧金山不如纽约和洛杉矶？首先因为城市小，好馆子总数自然少。其次房租和办证难逼得餐厅要么极贵要么极便宜，中间价位稀缺。
还有一个常被忽略的原因：市内交通太差，人们懒得跨区吃饭。餐厅只服务本地熟客，竞争少了，创新和提质的动力也就弱了。
他偏爱的三类馆子：伪居酒屋（小盘分享、在传统菜系上加异国配料）、人均 90 到 120 美元的「嬉皮士精致餐饮」、以及新开的廉价小店。
具体推荐包括 Maria Isabel、Prik Hom、Mijoté、Mr. Pollo、Khao Tiew、Timur 等。他也直言 La Taqueria、Saigon Sandwich 这些排队名店，其实不如附近不用排队的对手。
街区方面，Mission 是当之无愧的最佳觅食地，Chinatown 和 SoMa 最让人失望。这只是一份系列的第一篇，一年后他还会带来 Part 2。

en.thesis: San Francisco is not a food desert; its problems are size and cost, not cooking.
paragraphs: The author has lived in San Francisco for a decade and is tired of hearing that it is a food desert. He set out to eat across the whole city, and now thinks he can write a reliable guide.
His standard is 'yums per dollar': the more deliciousness you get for the price, the higher the rank. Anything above $150 a person is out, Michelin stars or not.

Why is SF worse than New York or LA? First, it is small, so the absolute number of great restaurants is lower. Second, rent and red tape push restaurants to either obscenely expensive or dirt cheap, leaving few mid-priced options.

A third, overlooked reason: the transit system is bad, so people rarely travel across town to eat. Restaurants serve their regular locals, competition weakens, and there is little incentive to innovate.
He favors three kinds of places: pseudo-izakayas (small plates, creative twists on a base cuisine), 'hipster fine dining' at $90 to $120 a head, and new cheap hole-in-the-walls.
Picks include Maria Isabel, Prik Hom, Mijoté, Mr. Pollo, Khao Tiew and Timur. He also calls out La Taqueria and Saigon Sandwich as overrated lines, when equally good places sit nearby without queues.
By neighborhood, the Mission is the best place to eat in the city; Chinatown and SoMa disappoint the most. This is only Part 1 of a series, with Part 2 coming in about a year.

articles.title: Fintech plus Education equals better outcomes for consumers
articles.titleZh: 金融科技加教育，等于消费者更好的结果
articles.author: Elisabetta Basilico, PhD, CFA

zh.thesis: 金融普惠的关键不是开户，而是让新手在反复使用中学会——工资直接入账就是最好的课堂。
paragraphs: 金融普惠常被看作访问问题：开了户、能转账就行。但很多新用户不敢用，怕出错、怕隐藏费用、怕被骗，账户开了也一直闲置。
一篇论文用无银行账户的工厂工人做实验：一部分人只开账户，另一部分人工资直接打入账户。结果，直接入账的人每月都要用，很快就学会独立操作。
他们学会了绕开收黑费的中间人，自己直接转账；对技术的信任也提高了，手机钱包与银行账户之间的信任差距几乎消失。
这些人存下更多钱，减少随意消费，也更能应对意外冲击。而只开了账户、仍拿现金工资的人进步小得多。关键是被使用，不是被拥有。
所以对理财顾问的启示是：信心来自经验。与其让客户先读一堆材料，不如带他们完成一次简单的转账。一次成功的操作，胜过长篇大论。

en.thesis: Financial inclusion is not about opening an account but about learning through repeated use — and direct wage deposits are the best classroom.
paragraphs: Financial inclusion is usually framed as an access problem: open an account, let people transfer money, and the rest follows. But many new users are too afraid to use it — mistakes, hidden fees, fraud — so accounts sit idle.

A field experiment gave unbanked factory workers accounts, but only some had wages paid directly into them. Those with direct deposit used the account every month and quickly learned to use it independently.
They learned to bypass agents who charged illicit fees and transact directly; their trust in the technology also rose. The trust gap between mobile money and bank accounts nearly disappeared.

These workers saved more, cut discretionary spending, and coped better with unexpected shocks. Those who merely had an account but still took cash wages improved far less. Active use, not ownership, is what matters.

So the lesson for financial advisors is that confidence comes from experience. Rather than handing clients a stack of readings, walk them through one simple transaction. A single successful operation is worth a long lecture.

articles.title: Glass eggs
articles.titleZh: 玻璃蛋
articles.author: Matilda Hay

zh.thesis: 玻璃蛋的比喻戳破了一个幻觉：我们总以为珍贵的东西可以既美又结实，其实它们往往最经不起碰。
paragraphs: 玻璃蛋是摆着看的物件：像蛋，却不能孵、不能吃，一碰就碎。作者从它入手，谈我们如何对待生命中那些脆弱的东西。
越珍惜，越容易用力过猛。攥紧它、反复检查它还在不在——玻璃蛋提醒你，这些动作本身就是伤害。
所以珍惜不是加固，而是学会轻放。承认它脆，接受它早晚会走，趁它还在的时候好好看着。

en.thesis: The glass egg punctures a comfortable illusion: we assume the things we treasure can be both beautiful and solid, when in fact they are usually the easiest to break.
paragraphs: Glass eggs are ornaments for the shelf: egg-shaped, but they cannot hatch, cannot be eaten, and break at a touch. The author uses one to talk about how we treat the fragile things in our lives.
The more we treasure something, the more we tend to overdo it. We grip it tight, keep checking that it is still there — and the glass egg reminds you that these very gestures are what hurt it.
So cherishing is not about reinforcement but about learning to set things down gently. Admit that it is fragile, accept that it will leave, and look at it properly while it is here.

articles.title: When it comes to inflation, ‘in’ is better than ‘out’
articles.titleZh: 论通胀，在内好过在外
articles.author: Joachim Klement

zh.thesis: 波兰、匈牙利、捷克都有自己的货币和央行，2022 年通胀却高于欧元区的斯洛伐克——小国的货币自主权只是名义上的。
paragraphs: 按理说，有本币和独立央行的国家，2022 年应该把通胀压得更低。但伦敦政经学者研究了波兰、匈牙利、捷克、斯洛伐克四国，发现正相反。
四国经济很像，都靠德国外包制造增长。唯一差别是斯洛伐克 2009 年加入欧元区，其余三国货币独立，加息也更快。
但它们的结果更差：通胀高于斯洛伐克，赤字和增长也没占优。原因在于 ECB——它像美联储主导全球一样主导全欧洲，体量太大，小国没法真正独立。
小国真想独立，投资者就对当地央行失去信心，通胀预期反而失锚。所以对这类小国来说，欧元区身份不是束缚，而是稳住通胀预期的锚。

en.thesis: Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic had their own currencies and central banks, yet saw higher inflation in 2022 than Slovakia — small countries' monetary autonomy is mostly nominal.
paragraphs: In theory, a country with its own currency and central bank should have fought the 2022 inflation spike better. Researchers at the London School of Economics compared Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic and Slovakia, and found the opposite.

The four economies look much alike — all lean on outsourced manufacturing from Germany. The one difference is that Slovakia joined the euro in 2009, while the other three kept their own currencies and hiked rates faster than the ECB.

Yet they did worse — higher inflation than Slovakia, with no better deficits or growth. The reason is the ECB: it dominates all of Europe the way the Fed dominates global markets, and it is simply too large for a small country to go truly independent.

If a small country genuinely tries to go its own way, investors lose confidence in its central bank and inflation expectations come unmoored. So for these countries, eurozone membership is not a straitjacket but an anchor for inflation expectations.

articles.title: Another California Court Has Now Broken Media Advertising, So The Copia Institute Asked Another California Appeals Court To Fix It
articles.titleZh: 又一家加州法院破坏了媒体广告，Copia Institute 于是请求另一家加州上诉法院来修复
articles.author: Cathy Gellis

zh.thesis: 按加州 Unruh 法案（反歧视法）把「广告没推给特定年龄用户」当成年龄歧视，既违反第一修正案，也违背 Section 230。
paragraphs: 加州上诉法院在 Liapes 诉 Facebook 案中裁定：广告不推给特定年龄用户，可能构成年龄歧视。Copia Institute 认为这不成立。
广告是言论，不是商品，反歧视法管不着；美国媒体一个多世纪靠广告活，按年龄挑受众是常态。Section 230 保护平台转述第三方内容，包括广告。
当年最高院拒绝复审。近日一家下级法院又放行了对 Google 的同类诉讼。Copia 多给一条理由：政府对言论定向的要求互相矛盾，第一修正案是防止表达者被夹在中间。
加州自己就矛盾：一边暗示按年龄拒发广告可能违法，一边又立法要求平台按年龄屏蔽内容。Copia 认为两套法律都违宪；正是这种拉扯，第一修正案必须护住表达者的选择权。

en.thesis: Treating a failure to show an ad to users of certain ages as discrimination under California's Unruh Act violates the First Amendment and ignores Section 230.
paragraphs: A California appeals court ruled in Liapes v. Facebook that failing to show an ad to users of certain ages can be age discrimination. The Copia Institute argues this is wrong.

An ad is speech, not a product, so anti-discrimination law does not reach it. American media has lived on advertising for over a century, and picking audiences by age is routine. Section 230 protects platforms passing along third-party content, and ads are that too.

The state's highest court declined to review the case back then. Now a lower court has let a similar claim against Google proceed. Copia adds a reason: government bodies contradict each other about how speech should be directed, and the First Amendment exists to keep speakers out of that tug-of-war.

California itself is torn: one law hints that refusing to show an ad based on age may be illegal, while new laws demand platforms block content based on age. Copia calls both unconstitutional — and that tug-of-war is exactly why the First Amendment must protect a speaker's choice of audience.

articles.title: 《雾海之下》的待机模式，你发现了吗？
articles.author: 林翔

zh.thesis: 《雾海之下》用「吃」串起搜集、成长和建设，把搜打撤的乐趣从「成功撤离」挪到了战斗本身。
paragraphs: 作者测试《雾海之下》时，无意间触发了待机模式：爵士乐响起，画面切到炉火旁的沙发，滑动滑块才能回到游戏。这个屏保式的小细节，成了首测里最深的印象之一。
首测阶段的游戏，有些东西完全可以「不那么完整」。但这款网易雷火织屋工作室的新作，连捏脸选的呆毛都会从帽子和发饰的缝隙里支棱出来。不影响核心玩法的细节，制作组也在认真打磨。
游戏的核心概念叫「吃打撤」：进图搜集、战斗、再撤离。开局吃下的魔法料理决定职业——曼德冰茶、武酪拼盘、铃兰初露对应牧师、战士和法师，测试版共 8 种职业可解锁。
传统搜打撤里，带出来的东西最终都换成卖价，玩家容易变得功利。这里食材能做料理、提升熟练度，素材进据点建设，高价值物品才拿去卖。于是带出来的每样东西都有去处。
战斗采用 MOBA 式俯视角，成都街头 163 名路人试玩，92% 无需教学就能上手。一局约 15 分钟。失败惩罚也轻：经验照常转化为职业熟练度，免费补给送一套不会损失的装备。
撤离不再是唯一的回报，玩家反而更愿意主动去打架。作者把它看作一次对品类边界的尝试：进入地图这件事，不再只是为了把背包安全带出来，战斗本身也值得。

en.thesis: 《雾海之下》 uses eating to tie looting, growth and base building together, shifting the fun of the extraction genre from a successful escape to the fight itself.
paragraphs: While testing 《雾海之下》, the author accidentally triggered its idle mode: jazz faded in, the screen cut to an empty sofa by the fireplace, and you slide a slider to get back in. This screensaver-like detail became one of the deepest impressions of the first playtest.

A first playtest is normally allowed to be incomplete. Not this one, from NetEase's Leihuo Zhiwu studio: even the little anime-style hair strand you choose in character creation keeps poking out from under hats and hair ornaments. Details that don't touch the core loop were still polished with care.

The core concept is 'eat, fight, extract': you enter the map to gather, fight, and extract. The magic dish you eat at the start decides your class — Mande Iced Tea, Warrior Cheese Platter and Lily Dew map to priest, warrior and mage, with eight classes to unlock in the beta.

In a traditional extraction game, everything you carry out eventually becomes a selling price, and players grow calculating. Here, ingredients make dishes and raise cooking skill, materials feed base construction, and only high-value items are sold for cash. So nothing you bring out feels useless.

Combat is a MOBA-style top-down view. A street test in Chengdu had 163 random passersby try the game, and 92% could play right away without a tutorial. A match runs about 15 minutes. Failure stings less: battle experience still feeds class proficiency, and a free supply crate gives you a set of gear you never lose.

With extraction no longer the only reward, players are more willing to pick fights. The author reads this as an attempt to push the genre's boundaries: entering a map stops being just about getting your backpack out safely — the fighting itself is worth it.

articles.title: James Joyces’s Baby Impressions and Other “Awkward Pleasures” of Literary Biography
articles.titleZh: 詹姆斯·乔伊斯模仿婴儿，以及文学传记的其他『别扭的乐趣』
articles.author: Daisy Hildyard

zh.thesis: 传记从来不是中立地带：讲一个人的一生，总得有人被点名、被羞辱、被责怪。
paragraphs: 文学传记是种别扭的乐趣。你会撞见乔伊斯模仿婴儿说话，或看到塞巴尔德年轻时的照片：赤膊站在河里，手持匕首。它也有实用处：作家怎么追稿费、孩子几点午睡。
赫敏·李是这类传记的典范，把原始研究和作品解读融在一起。她的《佩内洛普·菲茨杰拉德》《弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫》值得反复读，注释都能顺着查回出处。
访谈里最锋利的一段关于责怪。李说，传记跟责怪关系极大，它不是中立地带；讲一个人的一生，好像总得有人被责怪。两人也谈到谎言、秘密，以及不愿公开的事——李自己也守口如瓶。
《被画下的阴影》为救艾略特的前妻维维恩，把 T.S. 艾略特写成恶魔；写伍尔夫的传记总得挑个责任人：伦纳德、哥哥们，或父亲。所以读传记，读的也是作者的选择：救谁、怪谁。

en.thesis: Biography is never a neutral zone: telling a life story always ends with someone named, shamed, and blamed.
paragraphs: Literary biography is an awkward pleasure. You catch James Joyce doing a baby impression, or come across a photo of the young Sebald: bare-chested in a river, dagger in hand. It is practical too: you learn how writers chased their invoices and when their children napped.

Hermione Lee is the model for this kind of biography, fusing original research with readings of the work. Her Penelope Fitzgerald and Virginia Woolf reward rereading, and the footnotes lead you back to her sources.

The sharpest part of the interview is about blame. Lee says biography has a great deal to do with blame; it is not a neutral zone. Telling a life story, it seems, always ends with someone being blamed. They also talk about lies and secrets, about the parts of a life that stay hidden — Lee is reticent about her own.

Painted Shadow, written to rescue Eliot's first wife Vivienne, has to turn T. S. Eliot into a demon. A biography of Woolf must pick a culprit — Leonard, the half-brothers, or the father. So reading a biography is also reading its author's choice: whom to save, whom to blame.
